reference_sql:
SELECT campaign_id, channel_id,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_id) AS channel_campaigns
FROM campaigns
alternatives:
WITH channel_counts AS (  -- one row per channel with campaigns
  SELECT channel_id, COUNT(*) AS n_campaigns
  FROM campaigns
  GROUP BY channel_id
)
SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, cc.n_campaigns AS channel_campaigns
FROM campaigns c
JOIN channel_counts cc ON cc.channel_id = c.channel_id

SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaigns c2 WHERE c2.channel_id = c.channel_id) AS channel_campaigns
FROM campaigns c

other_way.sql:
WITH channel_counts AS (  -- one row per channel with campaigns
  SELECT channel_id, COUNT(*) AS n_campaigns
  FROM campaigns
  GROUP BY channel_id
)
SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, cc.n_campaigns AS channel_campaigns
FROM campaigns c
JOIN channel_counts cc ON cc.channel_id = c.channel_id
other_way.tradeoff: Counting per channel in a step of its own and joining it back works everywhere, but it reads the table twice.
